findings.claim: The dismiss_stale_reviews WARNING block added by fix-round-5 (lines 313–332 of enable-required-check.sh) uses the `log` function, which writes to stdout, not stderr. FIX-ROUND-5.md's SAFE-R3-003 closure description states 'the warning fires on stderr'; ADOPT-001 §12.7.3 (extended by COMP-R3-nit-002) references 'the helper's stderr WARNING when this is missing.' Both descriptions are factually incorrect: `log()` is defined at line 246 as `printf '[020G] %s\n' "$*"` with no stream redirection — it emits on fd 1 (stdout). Every other defensive WARNING in the script explicitly targets stderr: the PAT-scope warning at lines 106–108 uses `echo "WARNING: ..." >&2`; the no-enforce-admins block at lines 201–208 uses `echo ... >&2`. The dismiss_stale_reviews block is the sole exception.
findings.evidence: enable-required-check.sh line 246: `log() { printf '[020G] %s\n' "$*"; }` — stdout, no >&2; lines 106–108: `echo "WARNING: this script requires gh authenticated…" >&2` — stderr, consistent with script convention for operator-facing warnings; lines 201–208 no-enforce-admins block: `echo "WARNING: --no-enforce-admins applied…" >&2` — stderr; lines 327–331: `log "WARNING: required_pull_request_reviews.dismiss_stale_reviews is ${DISMISS_STALE_VAL}…"` — stdout via log(); FIX-ROUND-5.md SAFE-R3-003 closure row: 'The warning fires on stderr if the preserved review-shape has dismiss_stale_reviews: false or absent'; ADOPT-001 §12.7.3 (post COMP-R3-nit-002): 'Multi-maintainer adopters MUST also set dismiss_stale_reviews: true — see §12.7.4 for the security rationale and the helper's stderr WARNING when this is missing.'
findings.impact: In non-interactive operation — the operator runs `./enable-required-check.sh … > output.txt` to capture the invocation-log block emitted at the end of the script — stdout is redirected to the file and the dismiss_stale_reviews WARNING does not appear in the terminal, silencing it at the moment most likely to escape notice. The rest of the script's stderr warnings (PAT scope, no-enforce-admins) continue to reach the terminal because they are on fd 2. The failure mode is: operator captures the log block for pasting into branch-protection-log.md (a documented post-invocation step), sees no terminal warning about dismiss_stale_reviews, skips the follow-up UI configuration, and leaves the multi-maintainer Gate 1 partially open to the post-approval-push attack the warning was introduced to prevent. Additionally the documentation/implementation discrepancy ('stderr' in FIX-ROUND-5.md and ADOPT-001 §12.7.3, 'stdout' in code) will mislead future maintainers who rely on the documentation to understand the script's warning behavior. Severity is MIN not MAJ because the warning IS emitted (just on the wrong stream), and interactive invocations — the primary expected mode for this bootstrap-only script — do display the warning.
findings.mitigation: Replace the four `log "WARNING: …"` calls in lines 327–331 with `echo "[020G] WARNING: …" >&2` to match the script's established stderr pattern for operator-facing defensive warnings. Update FIX-ROUND-5.md and ADOPT-001 §12.7.3's 'stderr WARNING' references — both are already factually correct after this script change, so no doc change is needed beyond confirming the fix is in place. The jq filter, the WARNING text content, the single-operator-ignorable caveat, and the gh api PATCH command in the WARNING are all correct and require no change.
